ai_high_level_narrative_summary: This document outlines Giani.ai's process for converting document chunks into a knowledge base using a two-step RAG process.  The first phase involves summarizing chunks and generating metadata.  Large documents are handled via a map-reduce approach.  The second phase is the real-time retrieval process, which first identifies relevant documents and then extracts specific answers from within those documents.

Adaptive prompting is used to tailor the summarization and metadata extraction based on document type. Four prompt groups (Strategic, Research, Project Execution, and Conversational) are defined, each with specific metadata extraction targets.  The document also details the map-reduce process for handling large documents and provides example prompts for each group.

ai_main_topics_with_summaries_list_of_ob.topic_summary: This phase uses a two-step process to answer user questions. Step 1 identifies relevant documents based on high-level summaries. Step 2 extracts specific answers from chunks within those documents.
This section explains how Giani.ai uses adaptive prompting based on four document content groups (A, B, C, and D) to tailor summarization and metadata extraction.
This section details the map-reduce process for handling large documents, where the 'map' phase processes sections in parallel and the 'reduce' phase synthesizes the results.

ai_key_takeaways_bullets: Giani.ai uses a two-step RAG process for efficient and relevant information retrieval.
Adaptive prompting tailors summarization and metadata extraction based on document type.
A map-reduce approach handles large documents exceeding the LLM context window.
The system stores both chunk-level and document-level vectors for retrieval.
